checks: Read work_summary, out/q40/summary.txt and residuals.txt, and the Harada Table 13 rows (H13CO+ 1-0 = 9.4+-0.95, 3-2 = 2.6+-0.49 K km/s at N; HCN 197, HCO+ 205/91.6 K km/s). I did not re-run the fit. Reading the printed numbers, the 3-2/1-0 ratio of 0.28 is consistent with the stated 0.28+-0.06.
Agree qualitatively: the H13CO+ pair at N is the only new discriminating datum, and it favours the hot/low-n branch over the cold thick branch for X<=40.

Disagree with the strength of the claim. In residuals.txt (variant H, X=40) the best fit has band-scale offsets of -1.75/-1.90 and the cold fit -2.40/-2.80 (apparently sigma units of the 10%/15% priors). Roughly 10 of the dchi2=17 comes from the band-scale prior penalty, not from the 13C data. The 13C data themselves differ by only ~2.7 sigma (HCO+ 13C 3-2 model 3.9 vs obs 2.6+-0.49 K km/s). The 'excluded at >=4 sigma' wording is therefore not supported as stated.
Even the best fit pulls the shared band scales by about 2 sigma at every X (offsets -1.75 to -3.5 for H, up to -3.5 for A). The one-zone model is under tension before the 13C data are added.

Variant A (adding H13CN from the Q29 2.2'' maps) makes S fit badly (chi2 12-45 for X<=60), and S wants X>~90 while N wants 30-40. Either 12C/13C differs between N and S, or the beam and aperture mismatch and the one-zone model fail. This undermines 'X<=60 excludes the thick branch', because the same X cannot fit all three positions.
At X=60 the exclusion is only 5.2 (H) and the best N fit has chi2 12.7, so conclusions depend entirely on an unknown X. The summary says as much, but the headline should be conditional.

The intermediate branch (30<Tk<100 K) is much less excluded: dchi2 about 7 at X=40 and about 1 at X=60 (the 'best(30<Tk<100)' line). The hot solution sits at the Tk=300 K cap with n~10^4.7. The work shows Tk<=30 K is disfavoured, not that Tk is 170-300 K. The 'hot branch Tk 170-300 K' statement and the quoted N(HCN)/N(HCO+)=3.5 should be reported as a lower bound on Tk with the cap noted.

fixes.what: Decompose dchi2 (cold vs hot) into data terms (each 12C and 13C line) and prior terms (band scales, eta). Repeat with band scales free or widened to 20-25% and with the 13C lines' own calibration scatter added. Report the dchi2 purely from the 13C 3-2/1-0 ratio.
fixes.why: Much of the quoted 17-32 appears to come from the band-scale penalty rather than the 13C data. Without this the sigma values are not interpretable.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Report per-datum residuals (pull) in both branches and the likelihood ratio from the isotopologue ratio alone; marginalise nuisance scales with weak priors, and compute Bayes factors rather than dchi2 on a grid maximum.

fixes.what: Treat 12C/13C as a nuisance parameter with a justified prior (and let it differ between N and S). Constrain it from data in hand: 13CO/C18O is 2.4 at N in Table 13, and 13CO 2-1 and 1-0 are available, together with LIRG literature values (Henkel+14, Sliwa+17, Tang+19). Marginalise the cold-vs-hot evidence over X instead of stepping through 25-90.
fixes.why: The conclusion flips between X=60 and X=90, and the N and S data prefer different X. A conditional exclusion at fixed X is not a result about the branch.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Put a log-normal prior on X from independent isotopologue ratios, include optically-thin C18O and 13CO columns, and report the marginal posterior P(Tk<=30 K).

fixes.what: Remove or reconcile the beam mismatch. The Harada 1.7'' H13CO+ pair is combined with 12C lines at 1.7'' and H13CN taken from 2.2'' Q29 maps scaled onto the Harada 12C intensities. Test with all lines tapered to a common beam (the Q29 maps are already short-spacing complete) or restrict to H13CO+ only. Also address the HCO+ 3-2 and 1-0 filling-factor term, which is one shared eta here.
fixes.why: Scaling aperture ratios across different beams injects an unquantified systematic at the ~20% level, which is the size of the effect being tested. S fitting badly in variant A suggests exactly this.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Convolve to a common beam and extract spectra in the same aperture (matched-aperture ratios), then show the result is stable between taper choices.

fixes.what: Rephrase the headline and the reported finding. State the result as: Tk<=30 K, n>10^5.4 optically thick solutions are disfavoured at the dchi2 level shown, conditional on X<=40-60 and on the one-zone model. Do not state 'hot branch 170-300 K' and avoid the quoted N/S abundance significance beyond 2.1 sigma. Add a Tk-cap sensitivity (cap 500 K or none, plus a physical prior Tk<~150 K) and show whether the preferred branch moves to the intermediate 30-100 K solution.
fixes.why: Hits the cap, and intermediate temperatures are barely disfavoured. The N(HCN)/N(HCO+)=3.5 value depends on that branch.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Report one-sided limits at the prior boundary and show profile likelihoods in Tk.

notes_for_questioner: A matched-beam 1.7'' Band 3 H13CN and H13CO+ 1-0 map at S would fix the beam issue (uses the 1.7'' beam, needs the ALMA 3 mm data). The 13CO/C18O=2.4 at N implies strong 18O enhancement or 13C enrichment: ask whether 12C/13C at N is as low as 25-30, which also affects HCN/H13CN. Ask whether intermediate Tk (30-100 K) with HCO+ 13C self-absorption (shared eta) is still allowed once the band-scale penalty is removed.
